description:
FILED s449q (Opus round-7 agent Q), found while adding the `fcntl` builtin
(#592).  PRE-EXISTING and general â it is not about fcntl.

REPRODUCER:

    use IO::Handle;
    open(my $fh, '<', "/etc/hostname") or die;
    $fh->autoflush(1);          # perl: fine      PCL: dies
    my $n = $fh->fileno;        # perl: fine      PCL: dies

        perl  autoflush=ok  fileno=def  fileno-call=ok
        PCL   autoflush=ERR              fileno-call=ERR
              "Can't locate object method \"autoflush\" via package \"main\""

CAUSE: perl auto-blesses a lexical handle into a GLOB whose class is IO::File /
IO::Handle, so a method call on it dispatches.  PCL's `open my $fh` leaves the
raw CL STREAM in the box (see DECIDED Â§s326 "open() on a GLOB handle must not
overwrite the scalar"), which has no class at all â so the method resolver
falls back to the current package and dies.  The GLOB spellings DO work
(`IO::Handle->new`, `\*FH`, `Symbol::gensym`); it is exactly the modern
three-argument lexical form that does not.

WHY IT MATTERS: `$fh->autoflush(1)` and `$fh->print(...)` are the ordinary
modern idiom, and the s326 shim work made every IO::Handle METHOD available
without making them REACHABLE from the common handle shape.

FIX SHAPES, neither designed:
 (a) make the method resolver treat a box holding a STREAM as an IO::Handle
     invocant (the smallest change; the class is implied by the value's type,
     so nothing about open changes).  Check what `ref($fh)` must then answer â
     perl says "GLOB", so a ref() change would be a second, separate decision.
 (b) have `open my $fh` install a blessed glob the way perl does.  Bigger, and
     it re-opens the s326 box-representation ruling.

BAR: `$fh->autoflush(1)` / `->fileno` / `->print` / `->fcntl` / `->getline` on a
lexical handle vs perl; `ref($fh)` before and after; the s326 glob spellings
must not move; guard rows beside the existing IO ones in Pl/t/fileio-02.t.
subject: No IO::Handle method works on a plain lexical filehandle â `$fh->autoflush` / `->fileno` / `->fcntl` all die "Can't locate object method"
